description: Add --replay-only to you worker-sessions stream so operators can drain retained Worker Session events to redirect-safe NDJSON, receive an explicit completeness summary, and exit 0 without attaching a live follower, while preserving existing live-stream and ACTIVE transcript-read semantics.

context.customerAsk: Allow operators to run you worker-sessions stream --replay-only --output json against ACTIVE or terminal sessions, redirect retained events to a file, receive an explicit final completeness marker, and exit 0 without cancellation or live following.
context.problem: The existing stream replays retained events and then follows live until terminal or cancellation, so capturing an ACTIVE session through shell redirection requires cancellation that can truncate the pipe and cannot distinguish a partial capture from a complete transcript. The read command correctly refuses ACTIVE sessions and must continue doing so.
context.solution: Add a finite retained-history mode owned by Worker Sessions and the process-local Events service. It snapshots and emits retained events once in canonical order without registering a follower, appends a replay-summary with authoritative completeness and emitted count, validates live/replay flag conflicts before output or network access, and preserves all existing non-replay-only and read behavior without adding storage.

acceptanceCriteria: you worker-sessions stream --replay-only --output json works for ACTIVE and terminal Worker Sessions, emits retained events exactly once in canonical order, appends exactly one replay-summary record, and exits 0 without registering or waiting on a live follower.

An ACTIVE-session replay ends with kind replay-summary, complete false, reason session-active, and eventsEmitted N, while a terminal-session replay ends with complete true; in both cases eventsEmitted equals the number of preceding event records.

Every JSON-mode stdout line is independently valid JSON, event lines retain the existing Worker Session stream NDJSON contract, diagnostics remain on stderr, and a built-process redirection test proves the resulting file ends with the summary record.
Replay-only combined with --follow or any other mutually exclusive live-follow selection fails with a stable typed conflict error before network access, follower registration, or stdout output.

Existing behavior is preserved: stream without replay-only still replays then follows until terminal or cancellation, terminal replay is equivalent to the full retained history, and worker-sessions read still rejects ACTIVE sessions with WORKER_SESSION_TRANSCRIPT_ACTIVE.

Quality gate: the named focused verification command go test ./tests/functional/provider_sessions/cli -run '^(TestWorkerSessionsCLI|TestWorkerSessionsReplayOnlyRedirectsWellFormedNDJSON)$' -count=1 and make verify-fast pass; Typecheck passes; no NEW lint violations relative to current main, and the gates green on main (backend-size, pkg-maint, pkg-file-count, pkg-structure, vet) stay green; generated CLI/OpenAPI/client artifacts are synchronized if their authored contracts change.

The implementation/review loop continues until required CI is terminal and passing, all blocking PR conversation feedback is explicitly addressed, merge conflicts and shared-file changes are resolved, and the PR is actually merged; opening, approval, green CI, or merge readiness alone is not completion.

userStories.title: Capture an ACTIVE session without following

acceptanceCriteria: Given an ACTIVE Worker Session with retained observations, replay-only emits each retained event once in canonical position order and does not emit observations published after the retained snapshot boundary.
The command does not register, retain, or wait on a live subscription after the retained drain and exits 0 without operator cancellation.
The last JSON line is a replay-summary with complete false, reason session-active, and eventsEmitted equal to the number of preceding event records, including zero when no events are retained.

Retained reads and lifecycle classification remain explicit Worker Sessions operations over the injected process-local Events service; no storage, hidden global state, or secondary dependency construction is introduced.
Focused Worker Sessions service, transport, and CLI behavioral tests pass.

Tests pass

userStories.title: Report a terminal replay as complete
userStories.description: As an operator, I want replay-only streaming of a terminal Worker Session to identify itself as complete so a captured file can be trusted as the full retained transcript.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a terminal Worker Session, replay-only emits the same complete retained event sequence and ordering available to a normal terminal stream, then exits 0.

The final replay-summary has kind replay-summary, complete true, and eventsEmitted equal to the number of preceding event records; its reason value, if present, is stable and documents the terminal outcome without changing event records.

Stream without replay-only retains its current retained-then-live termination and cancellation behavior, and worker-sessions read continues to return WORKER_SESSION_TRANSCRIPT_ACTIVE for ACTIVE sessions.
Focused ACTIVE-versus-terminal lifecycle regression tests pass without sleeps or cancellation as the replay-only completion mechanism.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Verified terminal replay against the real in-memory Events service with deterministic Worker Session completion: canonical retained opening and terminal records are emitted in order, the lifecycle record is TERMINAL_REPLAY, one complete session-completed replay-summary reports eventsEmitted 2, and the subscription closes afterward. Added CLI coverage proving TERMINAL_REPLAY does not end replay-only before the final summary and the command returns success. Existing live terminal-stream and ACTIVE transcript-read regressions remain covered.

userStories.title: Reject incompatible live and finite modes before output

acceptanceCriteria: Combining --replay-only with --follow is rejected with a stable typed CLI conflict error and a non-zero usage or failure exit before any stdout bytes are written.
Conflict validation occurs before network access and before any retained read or live subscription side effect.
A valid invocation with neither replay-only nor an explicit conflicting selection preserves the existing live-stream default.
The authored CLI contract, generated command metadata, help, and handler binding expose the flags and conflict consistently; generated artifacts are regenerated rather than hand-edited.
Focused CLI parsing, error mapping, and zero-output/zero-request behavioral tests pass.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Produce a redirect-safe NDJSON capture
userStories.description: As an operator, I want the real CLI process to write replay-only output as well-formed NDJSON so shell redirection produces a durable, machine-readable partial or complete capture.
acceptanceCriteria: A process-boundary test invokes the built you CLI, redirects replay-only JSON stdout to a file, waits for exit 0, and parses every non-empty file line as exactly one JSON value.

The redirected file contains canonical event lines followed by exactly one final replay-summary; the summary count matches the event-line count and its completeness matches the session lifecycle used by the test.
The test proves replay-only completes without sending cancellation and that diagnostics or errors do not contaminate the redirected stdout file.

Operator-facing help or canonical reference documentation includes the redirect workflow and explains the complete marker, ACTIVE versus terminal meaning, and conflict with live following using real supported flags and output.
